cons: US caselaw focus limits international utility
Less generalist than Harvey for corporate transactional work
name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
pros: Deep Westlaw integration for US law
Established trust record in law firms
files: Legal documents, contracts, deposition transcripts, and production sets.
value: AI legal research and document analysis from Casetext, now part of Thomson Reuters. Deep integration with Westlaw and a long track record in US legal research distinguish it from newer entrants.
engine: Built on GPT-4 with legal-domain fine-tuning and Westlaw retrieval.
quality: Strongest on US common law. The Thomson Reuters integration gives it a sourcing depth other tools lack. Still requires lawyer review.
tagline: Legal AI from Thomson Reuters, strongest on US caselaw and legal research.
use_cases: US caselaw research and citation checking
Deposition preparation and key issue extraction from document productions
Contract analysis and quick-turn research memos
governance_note: Same professional responsibility framing as Harvey: the tool accelerates, the lawyer is still accountable. The Westlaw integration is specifically valuable for the sourcing chain, because a hallucinated citation is immediately checkable rather than requiring a separate lookup. Attorney-client privilege analysis for the data path applies as with any legal AI.
training_optout: Thomson Reuters / Casetext terms govern customer data use. Verify under the current agreement.
